His artistic trajectory is shaped by his examination of critical social and political themes in Colombia: from narco-trafficking and violence — often linked — to education, migration, decolonisation and the exploitation of natural resources. title: artport: A History of Internet Art
summary: artport: A History of Internet Art marks the 25th anniversary of artport, the Whitney’s online gallery space for commissions of net art, which launched in 2001. Since its inception, artport has presented a snapshot of the varied practices artists use to engage with an ever-evolving online environment. Taking place online and in the gallery, the exhibition tells a history of the evolution of net art over a quarter century and features more than 100 works commissioned specifically for artport.

title: Cottage Industry: The Val-Kill Furniture Shop

title: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
summary: Roy Lichtenstein changed the way we see images. One of the defining artists of the Pop art movement, he turned the visual language of mass culture, comics, advertising, consumer goods, and commercial printing into some of the most recognizable images of the twentieth century. His work looked cool, crisp, and machine-made, but was meticulously handmade, revealing an artist fascinated by how images are built, copied, enlarged, circulated, and made new.

title: Juan Sánchez: States of Liberation
summary: Juan Sánchez: States of Liberation will be the first traveling retrospective devoted to Juan Sánchez, one of the founding figures of Latinx art in the United States. For more than four decades, Sánchez has created a powerful and deeply personal body of work rooted in the histories, politics, and spiritual traditions of the working-class and Puerto Rican communities that shaped his upbringing in New York.
